# Choosing a class factory

robjc provides four factory functions for declaring R6 based classes and protocols.
Each returns a class generator.
Ordinary object classes and scalar classes create instances with `$new()`.
A singleton class also creates its shared instance when declared.
A protocol declares required method names; it is not a class for creating instances.

| What you need | Factory | What you use after declaration |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Ordinary object class | `RSObjectClass()` | `Class$new(...)` |
| Protocol specifying required methods | `RSProtocolClass()` | Pass `Class` in an adoption declaration |
| One shared instance | `RSSingletonClass()` | `Class$instance` |
| Scalar class wrapping an R value | `RSScalarClass()` | `Class$new(value)` and `Class$na` |

This guide explains how to choose a factory, its main arguments, and the behavior of the resulting class.
For the basics of instances and inheritance, see the [classes and objects guide](guide_02_Classes_Objects.Rmd).

## Shared arguments and class identity

`RSObjectClass()`, `RSSingletonClass()`, and `RSScalarClass()` take a class name in `class_name` and a parent generator in `super_class`.
Supply public and private fields and methods in `public` and `private`, and a list of adopted protocol generators in `protocols`.
A member cannot have the same name in both `public` and `private`.

`RSProtocolClass()` takes `protocol_name`, a list of parent protocols in `super_protocols`, and directly required method names in `contract_methods`.

All four factories also accept `parent_env` and `version`.
The default `parent_env` is usually sufficient.

The default `version` is `"1.0.0"`; the string cannot contain `_`.

The three object class factories also accept `validate_protocols`, which defaults to `TRUE`.
Class declaration stops if a required protocol method is missing.
Set it to `FALSE` to defer the check; the [Validate protocol contracts](#validate-protocol-contracts) section explains how to inspect missing methods later.

Class identity is not determined by name alone.
Declaring the same name twice creates two distinct classes.

```{r}
library(robjc)

First <- RSObjectClass("GuideSameName")
Second <- RSObjectClass("GuideSameName")
stopifnot(!identical(First, Second))
stopifnot(identical(First$new()$class(), First))
```

`RSObjectClass()` and `RSScalarClass()` do not accept a singleton as `super_class`.
For `RSScalarClass()`, the parent must also be `RSScalar` or one of its subclasses.
The parent of `RSSingletonClass()` must be a robjc object class.

The `version` value is stored in class identity metadata.
Registering a package class for archiving is separate from the factory arguments; see the [Archiving Guide](guide_10_Archiving.Rmd).

## `RSObjectClass()`

This is the basic factory for an ordinary class.
With no parent specified, the class inherits from `RSObject`.
Put public methods and fields in `public`, and internal state in `private`.
`$new()` allocates an instance, calls `initialize(...)`, and returns its result.
When defining `initialize()`, **call `super$initialize()` and return `self` when construction succeeds.**
Unlike ordinary R6 construction, robjc lets the initializer determine what `$new()` returns.

```{r}
Widget <- RSObjectClass(
  "GuideWidget",
  private = list(.label = NULL),
  public = list(
    initialize = function(label) {
      super$initialize()
      private$.label <- label
      invisible(self)
    },
    label = function() private$.label
  )
)
widget <- Widget$new("widget")
stopifnot(identical(widget$label(), "widget"))
stopifnot(identical(widget$class(), Widget))
```


## `RSProtocolClass()`

A protocol records required method names, not implementations.
It can inherit requirements from parent protocols through `super_protocols`.
A class declares adoption by passing the protocol generator in `protocols`.
It must provide the required methods itself or inherit them from a parent class.
`conformsTo()` checks the instance's adoption declaration; it does not repeat method validation when called.

```{r}
Labeled <- RSProtocolClass(
  "GuideLabeled",
  contract_methods = "label"
)
stopifnot(is.null(Labeled$new))

LabeledWidget <- RSObjectClass(
  "GuideLabeledWidget",
  protocols = list(Labeled),
  public = list(label = function() "labeled widget")
)
stopifnot(LabeledWidget$new()$conformsTo(Labeled))
stopifnot(identical(protocol_validateContracts(LabeledWidget), character(0)))
```

For protocol inheritance and adoption, see the [protocols guide](guide_03_Protocols.Rmd).

## Validate protocol contracts

With `validate_protocols = TRUE`, `RSObjectClass()`, `RSSingletonClass()`, and `RSScalarClass()` call `protocol_validateContracts()` during class declaration.
If a method is missing, the factory raises an error instead of returning a class. The following declaration fails because `label()` is absent.

```{r}
failure <- tryCatch(
  RSObjectClass("Guide05MissingLabel", protocols = list(Labeled)),
  error = identity
)
stopifnot(inherits(failure, "error"))
stopifnot(grepl("missing protocol methods: label", conditionMessage(failure), fixed = TRUE))
```

An inherited public method can satisfy a contract.
If a protocol inherits from another protocol, the parent's requirements are checked as well.
The validator checks the **names of public instance methods**. It does not verify arguments, return values, or behavior.

```{r}
LabeledParent <- RSObjectClass(
  "Guide05LabeledParent",
  public = list(label = function() "from parent")
)
LabeledChild <- RSObjectClass(
  "Guide05LabeledChild",
  super_class = LabeledParent,
  protocols = list(Labeled)
)
stopifnot(identical(protocol_validateContracts(LabeledChild), character(0)))
```

Use `validate_protocols = FALSE` when implementation must be deferred.
The adoption declaration still remains. Pass the class generator to `protocol_validateContracts(Class)` to get a character vector of missing names, or `character(0)` when none are missing.
Checking later does not supply the missing methods. Provide a class with those methods before relying on the protocol.

```{r}
DeferredWidget <- RSObjectClass(
  "Guide05DeferredWidget",
  protocols = list(Labeled),
  validate_protocols = FALSE
)
stopifnot(DeferredWidget$new()$conformsTo(Labeled))
stopifnot(identical(protocol_validateContracts(DeferredWidget), "label"))
```

All three object class factories perform this validation by default.
`RSSingletonClass()` checks before creating its shared instance.
`RSScalarClass()` checks both the regular class and its NA companion.
`RSProtocolClass()` **declares** contracts and therefore has no `validate_protocols` argument.

## `RSSingletonClass()`

This factory calls `$new()` while declaring the class to create the shared instance.
Therefore, **a custom `initialize()` must work without arguments and return `self`.**

```{r}
Registry <- RSSingletonClass("GuideRegistry")
stopifnot(identical(Registry$instance$class(), Registry))
stopifnot(identical(Registry$new(), Registry$instance))
```

After declaration, `$new()` returns the shared instance without running initialization again.
`robjc_allocate()` also returns that same instance for a singleton.
Use `Class$instance` to make the shared identity explicit.
`RSNull` is declared with this factory and also exposes its shared object as `RSNull$null`.
See the [singletons guide](guide_04_Singleton.Rmd) for its uses and behavior.

## `RSScalarClass()`

This factory creates a subclass of `RSScalar` and a companion subclass for NA values.
Pass a length-one missing value of the appropriate type in `na_value`.
The ordinary class exposes a shared NA instance as `Class$na`.

If you define `initialize(val)`, it must also accept `na_value` while the NA companion is being created.
To make `$new(NA)` return the shared NA instance, return the result of `super$initialize(val)` unchanged.

```{r}
Count <- RSScalarClass(
  "GuideCount",
  na_value = NA_integer_,
  public = list(initialize = function(val) {
    if (!is.integer(val)) stop("Expected an integer scalar.")
    super$initialize(val)
  })
)
stopifnot(identical(Count$new(2L)$value(), 2L))
stopifnot(identical(Count$new(NA_integer_), Count$na))
stopifnot(identical(Count$na$value(), NA_integer_))
stopifnot(identical(Count$na$class()$classname, "GuideCountNA"))
```

For a class name beginning with `RS`, the NA class is named `RSNA...`; otherwise `NA` is appended to the name.
By default, the NA class is a singleton whose `$new()` cannot be called.
Use `Class$na` instead.
With `na_singleton = FALSE`, an NA instance can retain information such as the levels and ordering of an `RSFactor` value.
For value wrappers and the difference between `NULL` and typed NA, see the [values and copying guide](guide_06_Values_Copying.Rmd).

## Choosing a factory

Choose `RSProtocolClass()` to declare required methods, or `RSSingletonClass()` for one shared object.
For a class wrapping a length-one R value, use `RSScalarClass()`; for other ordinary objects, start with `RSObjectClass()`.

The [class factory technical guide](tech_04_ClassFactory.Rmd) discusses how factories attach `isa` metadata and adjust `$new()` internally.
